processing: Pressed into a tuo, a small bowl-shaped nest. The details of its manufacture are little documented; it is treated as a Sichuan dark tea.
harvest_season: Little is recorded. Sichuan dark teas generally rely on mature leaf rather than an early picking.
appearance_dry: A dark, compact bowl-shaped tuo, as is typical of the form.
appearance_liquor: Probably dark reddish brown, as with other aged Sichuan dark teas.
appearance_wet: Dark brown leaf, typical of the class.
taste_profile: No dependable tasting record is available; expect the woody, earthy character common to Sichuan dark tea rather than any fixed profile.

brewing.notes: Typical for pressed dark tea: pry apart gently, rinse once, and use boiling water.

vintage_note: Known examples are sold by year in small pressed tuos, for instance a 100 g piece dated 2011. Stock is scarce and may go out of print, so a given year is hard to find again. Storage is worth asking about, as with any dark tea sold with age.
description:
Yibin Tuo Cha is a small bowl-shaped pressed dark tea from Yibin in southern Sichuan. It is seldom seen abroad, and known to most Western drinkers only through a few specialist sellers.

Little is documented about how it is made or who makes it. The shape is the same nest form made famous by Yunnan tuos, but that does not make it pu-erh.

Brew it as you would other pressed dark tea, with boiling water and a quick rinse. Since taste notes for it are scarce, your own tasting notes will count for more here than usual, and it is best bought in a small quantity first.
history: The tea's early history is not well recorded. What can be confirmed is its modern appearance on the market as a dated Sichuan pressed tuo, with a 2011 piece among the examples.
